judge_reasoning: The model's proposed infinite loop (Saheeli -2 -> Felidar token -> flicker original Felidar -> flicker Saheeli -> repeat) is vulnerable to a disruption the model failed to account for: after the first iteration, each subsequent Saheeli -2 activation reduces her loyalty to exactly 1 while the ability sits on the stack (since she resets to printed base loyalty 3 on each flicker, and -2 costs are paid immediately). Since loyalty abilities use the stack, the opponent can respond with a single Walking Ballista activation (dealing just 1 damage, well within the ≤2 damage capacity the model itself acknowledges remains available even after Shock) to kill Saheeli at this vulnerable moment, permanently ending the loop after only ~2 damage has been dealt. The model's contingency plan only covers the scenario where the opponent dumps all Ballista counters before Shock resolves, not this cheaper and more efficient mid-loop disruption. Recomputing the game state after this disruption shows the opponent survives at several life points, meaning the model's line does not guarantee a win against optimal opponent play, unlike the official solution which only requires Saheeli to survive exactly two activations (never triggering this vulnerability).
model_solution:
1. Play Island as your land for turn (you now have 5 untapped lands: 2 Spirebluff Canal, 2 Needle Spires, 1 Island).

2. Cast Shock, paying {R}, targeting Walking Ballista. This deals 2 damage to it (marked, not lethal to the 4/4). This "poisons" Ballista: from this point on, if the opponent ever removes even one +1/+1 counter for any reason, its shrinking toughness combined with the already-marked damage means it can never again produce more than about 2 total damage before it dies — nowhere near the 3 damage needed to kill Saheeli Rai at loyalty 3, or the 4 needed to kill Felidar Guardian.
   - (If instead the opponent responds to the Shock itself by immediately dumping 3–4 counters — the only window where Ballista is still fully healthy — see the contingency in step 6.)

3. Cast Felidar Guardian for {3}{W} using your remaining four lands (1 White from a Needle Spires, 3 generic from the rest). On its "enters the battlefield" trigger, exile and return one of your own tapped lands (a free, harmless untap) — do not target Whirler Virtuoso, so it stays available to attack later if needed.

4. Activate Saheeli Rai's −2 ability, targeting Felidar Guardian, creating a hasty artifact token copy of it.
   - The token entering the battlefield is an artifact entering under your control, so Reckless Fireweaver deals 1 damage to the opponent.
   - The token's copied "enters" trigger lets you exile Felidar Guardian and return it; Felidar's trigger fires again.
   - Use that second trigger to exile Saheeli Rai and return her. She re-enters as a brand-new permanent with 3 loyalty, having not yet activated a loyalty ability "this turn" as that new object.

5. Repeat step 4 (activate the newly-returned Saheeli's −2 again, chaining the blinks back through Felidar Guardian and then to Saheeli each time) as many times as necessary. Because Walking Ballista can never again assemble a 3-or-4-point single burst (per step 2), it cannot kill Saheeli Rai or Felidar Guardian to break the loop, and Winding Constrictor has no relevant activated ability. Each repetition triggers Reckless Fireweaver for another point of damage. Ten total repetitions take the opponent from 10 life to 0, ending the game during your main phase before you even need to attack.

6. Contingency: the only way the opponent can ever get a 3-damage burst out of Walking Ballista is to spend 3–4 of its counters on Reckless Fireweaver in response to your Shock, before Shock resolves (since only then is Ballista still a full 4/4). If they do this, Reckless Fireweaver dies, but Walking Ballista also dies in the process (either from removing all 4 of its own counters, or from Shock's 2 damage finishing off the shrunken body afterward). With Walking Ballista gone entirely, absolutely nothing can interrupt the Felidar Guardian/Saheeli Rai loop. In this case, simply run the loop from step 4/5 about ten times to generate ten hasty 1/4 artifact-token copies of Felidar Guardian (Reckless Fireweaver's damage no longer applies, but the loop itself is completely safe), then proceed to combat and attack with Spell Queller, Whirler Virtuoso, and all ten token copies. Winding Constrictor (the opponent's only remaining creature) can block at most one attacker, so at least 10 damage gets through regardless of how they block, which is lethal.

This line guarantees the opponent is reduced to 0 life this turn no matter how they choose to use Walking Ballista or block in combat.
